# The wire

const BRIDGE_VERSION = 1

## LaunchParams

```typescript
type LaunchParams = { readonly [key: string]: unknown }
```

Where inside an extension the user is: a deep link, replayed from
`location`. Its keys are the extension's own, which is why the bridge
cannot name them; an extension names them through `connect<P>()`.

## ParamsMessage

```typescript
interface ParamsMessage
```

Host → guest: the launch parameters changed under a mounted frame.

`params` used to arrive exactly once, inside `hello`, and there
was no way to send new ones. That is the difference between a
widget and a page: a page can be linked to, and a link that
resolves while the frame is already mounted had nowhere to land.
The host would have had to tear the frame down and rebuild it,
losing whatever state it held, to deliver a changed query string.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `igni` | field | `typeof BRIDGE_VERSION` | The wire's version: the same constant on both sides. |
| `kind` | field | `"params"` | Which message this is. |
| `params` | field | `LaunchParams` | Where inside the extension the user is now, changed under a mounted frame. |

## LocationMessage

```typescript
interface LocationMessage
```

Guest → host: where I am now.

*Not a navigation.** `navigate` asks the host to go somewhere
else; this says "I am still here, and here is now this". The host
folds it into its own URL and replays it in the next `hello`, so a
reload or a shared link comes back to the same place inside the
extension.

It exists because an extension has no other way to be addressable.
It cannot write the address bar — `allow-top-navigation` is
deliberately absent from the frame's sandbox — and it cannot
persist anything, because each extension is served from an
ephemeral port, a port is part of an origin, and so `localStorage`
is wiped whenever the backend restarts.

Strings only, and the host is free to cap or drop them: this ends
up in a URL, and an extension that puts its whole state here would
be writing an unbounded value into the host's address bar.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `igni` | field | `typeof BRIDGE_VERSION` | The wire's version: the same constant on both sides. |
| `kind` | field | `"location"` | Which message this is. |
| `nonce` | field | `string` | Issued per frame, per session. Every guest message must carry it. |
| `state` | field | `LocationState` | Where the user is, in strings, for the host to fold into its URL. |

## HostRequestMessage

```typescript
interface HostRequestMessage
```

Guest → host: one request to the host object model (`bridge.host…`).

The host side of the bridge forwards it to the backend with this
extension as the caller and its own window as the page's home, and the
backend checks it against the manifest's `permissions.host`. Nothing
here is trusted.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `igni` | field | `typeof BRIDGE_VERSION` | The wire's version: the same constant on both sides. |
| `kind` | field | `"host"` | Which message this is. |
| `nonce` | field | `string` | Issued per frame, per session. Every guest message must carry it. |
| `id` | field | `string` | Correlates the reply. Generated by the guest; echoed, never trusted. |
| `op` | field | `"get" | "set" | "call" | "subscribe" | "unsubscribe"` | What to do: read a property, write one, call a method, subscribe, unsubscribe. |
| `path` | field | `string` | `chat.processing`, `chat.post`; empty for subscribe. |
| `window` | field | `string | null` | A window other than this page's own, for `host.windows.ui(id)`. |
| `session` | field | `string | null` | A session other than the one on screen, for `host.sessions.chat(id)`. |
| `params` | field | `Record<string, unknown>` | The arguments of a call, by name. |
| `value` | field | `unknown` | The value of a write. |
| `signals` | field | `string[]` | Signal wire names, for subscribe and unsubscribe. |

## ServiceTokenMessage

```typescript
interface ServiceTokenMessage
```

Guest → host: a token for this extension's own service
(`bridge.service`).

Carries no audience, on purpose: the host asks the backend as this
frame's extension, and the backend answers for the service recorded
on that extension's own origin. A page cannot ask for anybody
else's.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `igni` | field | `typeof BRIDGE_VERSION` | The wire's version: the same constant on both sides. |
| `kind` | field | `"service-token"` | Which message this is. |
| `nonce` | field | `string` | Issued per frame, per session. Every guest message must carry it. |
| `id` | field | `string` | Correlates the reply. Generated by the guest; echoed, never trusted. |

## HostMessage

```typescript
type HostMessage = HelloMessage | ThemeMessage | ParamsMessage | ResultMessage | HostReplyMessage | HostSignalMessage | ServiceTokenReplyMessage
```

Anything the host says to a page.

The whole vocabulary of the host's side of the wire, in one union:
the greeting, the theme, the launch parameters, the answers to the
page's calls, the signals it subscribed to, and the tokens for the
extension's own service.

**Also** [`HelloMessage`](/docs/sdk/extension-bridge/reference-the-wire#hellomessage), [`ThemeMessage`](/docs/sdk/extension-bridge/reference-the-wire#thememessage), [`ParamsMessage`](/docs/sdk/extension-bridge/reference-the-wire#paramsmessage), [`ResultMessage`](/docs/sdk/extension-bridge/reference-the-wire#resultmessage), [`HostReplyMessage`](/docs/sdk/extension-bridge/reference-the-wire#hostreplymessage), [`HostSignalMessage`](/docs/sdk/extension-bridge/reference-the-wire#hostsignalmessage), [`ServiceTokenReplyMessage`](/docs/sdk/extension-bridge/reference-the-wire#servicetokenreplymessage).

## GuestMessage

```typescript
type GuestMessage = CallMessage | NavigateMessage | LocationMessage | CloseMessage | HostRequestMessage | ServiceTokenMessage
```

Anything a page says to the host.

The whole vocabulary of the guest's side of the wire: the calls it
makes, where it wants to go, where it is, that it is finished, the
host-model requests it makes, and the service token it hands back.

**Also** [`CallMessage`](/docs/sdk/extension-bridge/reference-the-wire#callmessage), [`NavigateMessage`](/docs/sdk/extension-bridge/reference-the-wire#navigatemessage), [`LocationMessage`](/docs/sdk/extension-bridge/reference-the-wire#locationmessage), [`CloseMessage`](/docs/sdk/extension-bridge/reference-the-wire#closemessage), [`HostRequestMessage`](/docs/sdk/extension-bridge/reference-the-wire#hostrequestmessage), [`ServiceTokenMessage`](/docs/sdk/extension-bridge/reference-the-wire#servicetokenmessage).

## isGuestMessage

```typescript
function isGuestMessage(data: unknown): data is GuestMessage
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data` | `unknown` | required | the message as it arrived, in whatever shape it is. |

Is this a message from a guest, shaped the way we require?

Written as a narrowing guard rather than a schema check because the
host has to answer this about `unknown` arriving from a frame, and
the answer has to be "no" for everything that is not exactly right.
A message that fails here is dropped without a reply: a guest that
can tell malformed from unauthorised has learned something.

**Also** [`GuestMessage`](/docs/sdk/extension-bridge/reference-the-wire#guestmessage).

## methodAllowed

```typescript
function methodAllowed(method: string, allow: readonly string[],): boolean
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `method` | `string` | required | the method the extension wants to call. |
| `allow` | `readonly string[]` | required | the methods it was granted, as exact names or as `*`-suffixed prefixes. |

May this extension call this method?

Exact names, or a `*`-suffixed prefix. No regular expressions and no
`*` anywhere but the end: a permission list is read by whoever
approves an install, and a pattern language it cannot be read in is
a permission nobody actually granted.
